title: Cross-Functional Incident Rehearsal and Customer Liaison Playbook
author: Priya Nambiar
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a repeatable, cross-functional incident rehearsal (game day) and operational playbook that foregrounds the Customer Liaison role. It covers the lifecycle from detection to postmortem for incidents that materially affect customer-facing inference throughput, latency SLOs, or safety/fidelity regressions.

Audience: SRE, Platform, Support, Solutions Engineering, Product, and Customer Success.

Scope: Tiered incidents that meet the criteria in the Incident Classification Matrix below (Severity 1/2/3 definitions). This playbook focuses on coordination patterns, customer status messaging cadence, role responsibilities, and rehearsal scenarios.

When to use this playbook

- Use as the runbook for multi-team incidents affecting customer SLAs, persistent latency regressions, or sustained model-quality regressions.
- Use as the template for scheduled game days and for onboarding customer liaison participants.

Incident classification matrix\n
| Severity | Customer impact examples | Immediate actions | SLO/threshold examples | Typical escalation path |
|---------:|-------------------------|-------------------|------------------------|-------------------------|
| Sev 1 | Platform outage for hosted API (multiple regions) or Dedicated capacity unavailable | Bridge & all-hands, customer status within 15m | Availability < 99.5% or P99 latency > 5s global | Pager -> SRE lead -> Eng oncall -> Exec notif |
| Sev 2 | Significant feature degradation affecting subset of customers | Triage, partial mitigation, status within 30m | Error rate spike > 5% sustained, single-region P95 latency > 3s | Pager -> Platform -> Customer Liaison -> Product |
| Sev 3 | Intermittent customer-facing anomalies, low-impact regressions | Owner assigned, customer outreach as needed | Error rate < 1% but user-visible | Slack alert -> Product/Support owner |

Roles and responsibilities

1) First Responder (FR): Acknowledges pager, collects signals, performs initial isolation.
2) Bridge Lead (BL): Runs the incident bridge, manages the timeline, and coordinates technical responders.
3) Customer Liaison (CL): Primary interface with customer success and affected customers. Crafts status page and email templates; owns customer-facing timing and tone.
4) Engineering SME: Implements fixes, triage, hotfixes, and rollback decisions.
5) Ops/Infra Lead: Evaluates capacity/fleet impacts and triggers failover or autoscaling policies.
6) Postmortem Author: Captures timeline and RCA within 72 hours.

Customer Liaison normative behavior

- Immediately after Bridge is stood up, CL posts initial customer-facing statement: acknowledgement, estimated scope, and next update window.
- Use empathetic language; avoid technical jargon in public statements. Example template in the Communications Templates section.
- Coordinate all external communications through the Support lead and the Legal/PR escalation path for regulated customers.

Quick triage checklist (first 15 minutes)

1. Confirm incident severity using the Incident Classification Matrix.
2. Gather key telemetry: P95/P99 latencies, error rates, request volume, KV cache hit rates, model-serving queue depth.
3. Capture impacted routes/models/customers.
4. Determine immediate mitigation: route traffic to fallback model, increase burst capacity, or enable cached responses.
5. CL posts initial status update (see templates).

Containment and mitigation run steps (example ordered list)

1. Stop-new-deploys: Initiate emergency change freeze in CI/CD.
2. Scale mitigation: Trigger autoscaling group increase or warm spare pool.
3. Model fallback: Switch affected route to verified lower-latency model variant with documented quality delta.
4. Traffic shaping: Apply rate-limits or queue backpressure for noisy tenants.
5. KV cache invalidation only if necessary and with caution (note: invalidation can increase load).
6. If root cause appears to be kernel/cuda or host-level degradation, move workload to healthy hosts and coordinate with cloud provider.

Runbook snippets and useful commands

- Dashboards to open: /dashboards/inference-overview, /dashboards/latency-by-model, /dashboards/cache-hit-rates, /dashboards/slo-violations
- Example kubectl to identify pod restarts: kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide --show-labels | grep serving
- Example curl health check: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.com/v1/healthz?model=redwood-l1
- Redis cache hit rate query (PromQL): sum(rate(redis_command_hits_total[1m])) / sum(rate(redis_command_calls_total[1m]))

Customer status page cadence and templates

Principles:
- Timing: initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes (Sev1), updates at predictable intervals (every 30–60 minutes for active incidents), and resolution notice within 30 minutes of service restoration.
- Content: short headline, impact summary, mitigation steps, next update ETA.
- Tone: accountable, clear, and non-technical for public posts.

Public status template (short)

- Title: We are investigating elevated API errors affecting text generation in US region
- Time: 2026-03-05 14:07 UTC
- Impact: Customers in the US region may experience increased error rates and longer response times.
- Mitigation: Traffic is being routed to healthy capacity and a rollback to last-known-good model is in progress.
- Next update: 15–30 minutes

Customer email template (for impacted customers)

Subject: Service disruption affecting Redwood inference (US region)

Hi <CustomerName>,

We’re currently investigating an issue impacting inference requests in the US region that may cause higher error rates and slower responses for some requests. Our SRE and Platform teams have an active bridge and are executing mitigations to restore service.

What we’re doing: routing requests to fallback capacity and rolling back a recent model variant to a verified version.

Next update: We will follow up in ~30 minutes or sooner with progress. If you require immediate assistance, reply to this email and we will prioritize you for direct support.

Thanks for your patience,
Customer Liaison, Redwood Inference

Internal Slack broadcast template

#incident-sev1: Initial ack — Bridge: <link> | Impact: US region errors | CL: @Priya | Next update in 15m

Postmortem guide and required artifact checklist

Required deliverables (due timeline):
- Preliminary timeline (published inside 24 hours)
- Full postmortem with RCA and mitigations (within 72 hours)
- Action items with owners and dates (tracked in the incident backlog)

Postmortem structure (use for every Sev1/2):
1. Summary (one-paragraph customer-facing)
2. Impact (who/what/when)
3. Timeline (UTC timestamps; include monitoring alerts and key commands executed)
4. Root cause analysis (include why detection/mitigation failed)
5. Corrective actions (short-term & long-term)
6. Confidence & test plan for each corrective action
7. Follow-ups and owners (Jira/Issue IDs)

Game day (rehearsal) plan template

Objective: Validate cross-functional choreography (SRE + Platform + Support + CL) for model-serving outages and customer comms.

Duration: 120–180 minutes

Participants and pre-reads:
- Bridge Lead (SRE)
- Customer Liaison (CS or Support)
- Engineering SME (Platform/Serving)
- Observability engineer
- Product owner and Solutions Engineer

Exercise flow:
1. Warm-up (10m) — Review roles, tools, and playbook pages.
2. Scenario kickoff (5m) — Inject a simulated upstream model artifact corruption that causes model mismatch and elevated error rates for a subset of customers.
3. Active response (60–90m) — Teams run the incident, practice mitigation (roll back model, adjust routing), and exercise the CL templates.
4. After-action (30–45m) — Immediate hot-wash: capture timeline, identify gaps in tooling/permission, and log action items.
5. Retro (15–30m) — Assign owners for improvements and schedule follow-ups.

Scoring rubric (example):
- Initial customer acknowledgment posted within target window (0/5)
- Technical mitigation applied and validated (0/10)
- Postmortem skeleton published within 24h (0/5)
- Clear owner assignment for all action items (0/5)

On-call rotation guidance and handoff checklist

Rotation lengths:
- Primary pager: 7 days (preferred) or 14 days max
- Secondary/backup: 14 days

Handoff checklist (pre-shift):
- Confirm coverage and contact details in the rota tool.
- Share outstanding low/medium action items and any running tickets.
- Verify access to key runbooks and dashboards.
- CL handover: the outgoing Customer Liaison shares open customer tickets and scheduled notifications.

Handoff checklist (post-shift):
- Document any incidents/near-misses that occurred during shift.
- Update on-call notes page with ongoing mitigations and ETAes.
- Acknowledge receipt in the rota tool.

Training and onboarding for Customer Liaisons

- New CLs complete two shadowing sessions across two live rotations and one replayed game day.
- Required reading: incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026 (internal), SLO definitions, and the customer-communication-tonebook.

Tooling and permissions matrix (table as text)

- PagerDuty: ack/resolve (roles: FR, BL) | Owner: SRE | Permission: oncall group
- Statuspage: publish/update (roles: CL) | Owner: Support | Permission: status-editor
- Jira: create incident tasks (roles: BL/PO) | Owner: Eng Ops | Permission: incident-writer
- Observatory dashboards: read/update (roles: all responders) | Owner: Observability | Permission: team-read

Appendix B — Glossary of common terms

- CL: Customer Liaison
- BL: Bridge Lead
- KV cache: Key-Value cache used for prefix caching
- P95/P99: 95th/99th percentile latency
